HI-2026-SB847.title: RELATING TO PSYCHOLOGISTS.
HI-2026-SB847.summary: Establishes a three-year pilot program in the County of Kauai and County of Hawaii to allow qualified psychologists under the supervision of a supervising physician or psychiatrist limited authority to prescribe certain psychotropic medications to patients between the ages of 18 and 65 years under the care of the psychologist. Requires the Board of Psychology to adopt rules. Requires the State Health Planning and Development Agency to report to the Legislature. (CD1)

actions.text: Received.

HI-2026-GM1362.aiSummary: Signed into law on July 15, 2026, this act updates Hawaii rules for electric bicycles, mopeds, and electric motorcycles. It sets safe riding rules for e-bikes, bars high-speed electric devices from public roads and paths, and says road-legal electric bicycles do not need insurance. It also requires labels, warning signs, and buyer info for electric bikes, and it bans mopeds and electric motorcycles from bike lanes and bike paths.

HI-2026-SB2852.title: RELATING TO CIVIL RIGHTS.
HI-2026-SB2852.summary: Requires the Hawaii Civil Rights Commission to adopt rules on digital accessibility for places of public accommodation that are consistent with certain federal regulations. Specifies that a violation of the rules is an unlawful discriminatory practice. Establishes that it is an unlawful discriminatory practice for a place of public accommodation to deny a person with a disability full and equal enjoyment of their goods, services, facilities, privileges, advantages, or accommodations, or information related thereto, by requiring the use of information and communication technology that is not accessible to the person. (CD1)

HI-2026-HB2338.title: RELATING TO THE HAWAII COMMUNITY COLLEGE PROMISE PROGRAM.
HI-2026-HB2338.summary: Addresses the change in federal law regarding Pell Grants by amending the Hawaii Community College Promise Program (Hawaii Promise) to provide scholarships for ninety-five percent of a student's unmet direct cost need and exclude grants, scholarships, and other funding sources from the calculation of Hawaii Promise awards, thereby allowing students to apply such funds toward indirect costs, including housing, food, and other living expenses, to reduce financial barriers and support student success. Changes Hawaii Promise from being a last-dollar award. Authorizes Hawaii Promise to coordinate with federal student aid programs to maximize total financial assistance available to students. Effective 7/1/2026. (CD1)

HI-2026-HB2338.aiSummary: The law changes the Hawaii Community College Promise Program so it can cover 95% of a student’s unmet direct college costs. It also stops counting other grants and scholarships in that award amount, so students may use those funds for other living costs like housing and food. It takes effect on 7/1/2026.

HI-2026-HB1753.title: RELATING TO SOCIAL MEDIA.
HI-2026-HB1753.summary: Requires certain social media platforms to provide an accessible mechanism for users to delete their accounts on the platform and permanently erase all personal information and sensitive personal information associated with deleted accounts. Prohibits certain deceptive practices by social media platforms that obstruct the deletion of user accounts. Authorizes the Attorney General to pursue civil actions and seek injunctive relief and penalties for violations. Effective 7/1/2027. (CD2)

HI-2026-GM1344.title: Informing the Legislature that on July 13, 2026, the Governor signed the following bill into law: HB1891 HD1 SD1 CD1 (ACT 242).

actions.text: Received.

HI-2026-GM1344.aiSummary: The governor signed this education bill into law as Act 242 on July 13, 2026. Starting with the 2028-2029 school year, Hawaii Department of Education schools must give approved dyslexia-aware reading screenings to students in kindergarten through grade 3 and to new students entering a school for the first time in the state. Schools must also provide evidence-based help for students flagged with dyslexia or reading problems, and the department must offer teacher training in structured reading instruction and work with teacher training programs.

HI-2026-GM1320.title: Informing the Legislature that on July 9, 2026, the Governor signed the following bill into law: HB1864 HD2 SD2 CD1 (ACT 218).

actions.text: Received.

HI-2026-GM1320.aiSummary: The governor signed this measure into law as Act 218. It requires health insurance and health plan contracts issued or renewed in Hawaii after December 31, 2026, to cover standard fertility preservation services for people who may have infertility from certain medically needed treatments, such as cancer treatment. It also bars insurers and plans from denying that coverage based on a prior diagnosis, past fertility treatment, or certain health factors.
